bio: Dr. Nkurunziza Joseph Ryarasa, MD, is a medical doctor and public health practitioner who has successfully bridged the gap between healthcare and social justice. He earned his medical degree from the National University of Rwanda and advanced his training with postgraduate qualifications in public health and HIV/AIDS care from the University of Roehampton, Antwerp, and UC San Diego.

His deep commitment to healthcare is reflected in his roles as Clinical Services Director for Drew Cares International and as a Clinical Services Specialist for the DoD/US Embassy Rwanda. He also co-founded and served as Board Director at the Health Development Initiative (HDI) Rwanda, an organization dedicated to improving the health of vulnerable populations.

His current governance work as the Executive Director of Never Again Rwanda (NAR) stems directly from his medical career. Through his public health practice, he recognized that clinical treatments alone cannot fix health inequities without addressing underlying structural issues. He now applies his healthcare leadership skills to champion good governance, human rights, and accountability as essential pillars for both social justice and a healthier public.
